verdict: Disney grew revenue 7% to $25.2B and segment profit 21% — streaming and parks both delivered — but an $812M writedown on its A+E stake, and comparison against last year's one-off tax benefit, cut reported EPS to $1.51.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $2.92 — last year had a one-off tax benefit

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Streaming subscriptions, TV network fees, park admissions, hotel rooms and cruises — the recurring heart of Disney.

segments.name: Products
segments.note: Merchandise, food and drinks sold at the parks, resorts and stores.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Marketing the movies, shows and parks, and running the company — down 4% YoY.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: The wear and tear on parks, cruise ships and equipment, spread over their working lives — up 6% YoY.

opex.name: Restructuring & impairment charges
opex.note: Mostly an $812M writedown of Disney's stake in A+E Networks — see the one-time items below.

takeaways.title: Entertainment profit jumped
takeaways.text: Entertainment operating income rose 64% to $1.68B as streaming grew, lifting total segment profit 21% to $5.6B — well ahead of Disney's own guidance.

takeaways.title: Parks kept packing them in
takeaways.text: Experiences profit rose 20% to $3.0B, with spending per guest up 4% — helped by roughly $100M of tariff refunds booked in the quarter.

takeaways.title: Sports had a soft quarter
takeaways.text: Sports profit fell 17% to $858M: short NBA playoff series and a TV carriage dispute cost more than higher subscription and ad fees added.

otherDetail: Other expense of $215M, net — $298M of net interest expense on Disney's debt, partly offset by $83M of equity income from companies Disney part-owns (such as Hulu).
footerNote: Segment operating income: Entertainment $1,680M, Sports $858M, Experiences $3,017M (before corporate costs). Of the $2,844M of net income, $206M belongs to noncontrolling partners; $2,638M is attributable to Disney shareholders.
follow100Note: Of the $11.27 kept as profit per $100 of revenue, about $0.82 belongs to noncontrolling partners — $10.45 is Disney shareholders'.
oneTimers: Restructuring and impairment charges were $900M, dominated by an $812M writedown of Disney's 50% stake in A+E Global Media — which Disney has agreed to sell to Hearst for about $1.2B.
The year-ago quarter included a one-time $2.7B income-tax benefit, which is why reported EPS fell from $2.92 to $1.51 even though pre-tax profit rose 14%.
